name: Zebulun
overview: Zebulun, named by Leah as a sign of dwelling, is one of the six sons she bore to Jacob, establishing a foundational tribe of Israel (Genesis 30:20; 35:23). His descendants formed a distinct tribe, with sons Sered, Elon, and Jahleel (Genesis 46:14), and were allotted a territory described as a haven by the sea, bordering Zidon, highlighting their maritime significance (Genesis 49:13). Zebulun is consistently mentioned alongside Issachar and Benjamin, emphasizing its integral role within Israel's tribal structure (Exodus 1:3). Although specific details about their camp placement are not given for Zebulun, the organization of Israel's camp, such as Judah's eastward position under Nahshon, frames the tribal arrangement in which Zebulun participated (Numbers 2:3).
